initialContact.message: I'm approaching retirement and concerned about healthcare costs. Right now I have occupational healthcare through the bank - free doctor visits, specialists, everything covered. When I retire, I lose that and go to public healthcare system. Should I get private health insurance for retirement? I'm 62 and healthy now, but I know healthcare needs increase with age. What do most retirees do?

problemContext.currentSituation: Bank manager approaching retirement worried about losing occupational healthcare
problemContext.emotionalState: planning ahead, concerned about future costs, cautious

idealAdvice: Smart to think about this before retiring - healthcare is major retirement factor
What you're losing:
Occupational healthcare: Fast access, specialists, preventive care, minimal cost
What you're getting:
Public healthcare (Kela system): Same quality care, longer waits, small fees
Finnish public healthcare for retirees:
- Doctor visits: ~20-25€
- Specialist after referral: ~40€
- Medications: Kela reimbursement (40-100% depending on type)
- Hospital care: Daily fee ~50€, capped annually
- Annual maximum out-of-pocket: ~700€/year, then free
This is actually quite affordable compared to many countries!
Private health insurance in retirement:
Age 62: Premiums 100-150€/month = 1,200-1,800€/year
Age 70: Premiums 150-250€/month = 1,800-3,000€/year
Age 75: Premiums 200-350€/month = 2,400-4,200€/year
Pre-existing conditions: Often excluded or expensive add-ons
What private insurance gives:
- Faster access (no waiting lists)
- Choose your doctor/specialist
- Better facilities (private hospitals)
Cost-benefit analysis for your situation:
If you use healthcare moderately: Public system costs ~1,000-2,000€/year
Private insurance costs: 1,800-3,000€/year (and rising with age)
Unless you need frequent specialist care: Public is more cost-effective
Recommendation:
Start retirement with PUBLIC healthcare only - try it for 2 years
Put 150€/month you'd spend on insurance into healthcare savings account
If you find waits unbearable or need frequent care: Reassess private insurance
Important: Apply for private insurance BEFORE retiring if you want it
Once you have health issues, harder to get coverage/more expensive
Many Finnish retirees: Use public for routine care, pay private out-of-pocket for urgent specialist visits
This hybrid: More flexible than insurance, often cheaper
With 85k€ in savings and good pension: You can afford to self-insure for healthcare
For you specifically: Public healthcare is likely sufficient, private insurance is peace-of-mind luxury
commonMistakes: Pushing private insurance without explaining public system quality
Not mentioning insurance gets expensive with age
Failing to explain annual out-of-pocket maximum in public system
Missing hybrid approach (public + pay private when needed)
Not advising to apply before retiring if he wants insurance
Scaring him about public healthcare waits (they're manageable for most)
